hook: The cleric who led the Iranian Revolution and founded the Islamic Republic.

pages.x: Ruhollah Khomeini was born in 1902 in the small town of Khomein, in Iran. His father was killed when he was a baby. He studied Islamic law and philosophy, and became a respected teacher in the holy city of Qom.
In 1963 he attacked the Shah's Western-style reforms and his ties to America and Israel. He was arrested, and in 1964 sent into exile.
He lived in exile in Turkey, then for 13 years in the holy city of Najaf, in Iraq, and finally near Paris. His sermons were recorded on cassette tapes, smuggled into Iran and copied by the thousand.
In 1978 vast protests and strikes spread across Iran, and in January 1979 the Shah fled. On 1 February Khomeini flew home to Tehran, where millions turned out to greet him.
After a referendum he founded the Islamic Republic, with himself as Supreme Leader. Opponents, including many former allies, were jailed or executed, and women were made to cover their hair.
In November 1979 students stormed the American embassy in Tehran and held 52 Americans hostage for 444 days, with Khomeini's backing.

In 1980 Iraq invaded Iran. The war lasted eight years and killed hundreds of thousands. Khomeini accepted a ceasefire in 1988, saying it was worse than drinking poison. That year thousands of political prisoners were executed.
In 1989 he called for the death of the British writer Salman Rushdie over his novel The Satanic Verses. Khomeini died that June, and millions mourned at his funeral.
Khomeini led the revolution that ended Iran's monarchy and created the Islamic Republic, a state ruled by clerics that still governs Iran.
pts: Founded the Islamic Republic of Iran
